name: Lying leg raise
pattern: Lower-body-first flexion: lying on your back, the legs lift and the pelvis curls toward the ribs while the trunk resists arching.
setup: Lie on your back, legs straight, arms by your sides or hands holding a bench behind your head.
Brace gently and set your low back flat-ish against the floor.
Point your toes lightly, legs together.

steps.text: Lift both legs together until they point at the ceiling.
At the top, roll your hips a little off the floor, tailbone toward the ceiling.
Lower the legs slowly; stop before your low back starts to arch.

cues.cue: Keep the low back down as the legs lower.
cues.why: Leg raises strongly fire the psoas, which pulls the lumbar spine into an arch and compresses it.

cues.cue: Finish by curling the hips up, not just swinging the legs.
cues.why: Hip lift (reverse crunch) is what brings in the abdominals; reverse crunches rank high for abdominal activity.

cues.cue: Lower only as far as you can keep your back still.
cues.why: Long straight legs make a large lever on the spine; bend the knees to shorten it.

cues.cue: Slow down on the way down.
cues.why: Dropping the legs uses momentum and lets the back arch.

breathing: Breathe out as the legs rise and the hips curl, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Lift in 1 second, lower in about 3.

mistakes.name: Low back arches
mistakes.looks: A gap opens under the low back as the legs come down.
mistakes.fix: Bend the knees, or stop higher; press the low back toward the floor.
mistakes.why: The hip flexors pull the spine into extension when the abs cannot hold it.

mistakes.name: Legs only, no hip lift
mistakes.looks: Legs swing to vertical but the pelvis never leaves the floor.
mistakes.fix: At the top, push the feet to the ceiling and lift the tailbone.
mistakes.why: It stays a hip flexor exercise.

mistakes.name: Dropping the legs
mistakes.looks: Legs fall fast and bounce off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Count three on the way down; tap, don't bounce.
mistakes.why: Momentum replaces muscle and jars the back.

safety: Low back pain: start with bent-knee reverse crunches or dead bugs; straight-leg lowering loads the spine.
Hip flexor or groin pain: shorten the range and bend the knees.

variants.change: Bent knees shorten the lever: easier on the back.
Head higher than hips on a decline bench: harder; a 30 degree inclined reverse crunch is among the highest abdominal exercises measured.
Legs stay low and move in small fast alternating kicks; keep the low back still.
Arms and legs lift together and meet over the hips: a whole-body fold.
Seated, leaning back on the hands, knees pull in and push out.

subtypes.name: Reverse crunch
subtypes.match: reverse crunch|hip raise|tuck crunch|leg.hip raise|hip lift|bottoms|pull in|knee raise
subtypes.change: Knees bent about 90 degrees; curl the hips off the floor.

subtypes.name: Flutter and scissor kicks
subtypes.change: Legs low, about a hand off the floor, kicking up and down in small alternating beats.

subtypes.name: V-up and jackknife
subtypes.change: Arms overhead to start; arms and legs lift together and meet over the hips.

motion.basis: Hip and pelvis angles estimated from the technique; psoas-driven lumbar extension risk from juker1998. Inclined reverse crunch ranking from escamilla2006.
